title: AI rout drags S&P 500 and Dow into correction; Nasdaq suffers worst week since 2020
content:
An AI-led sell-off deepened on Friday, with the S&P 500 falling about 3.7% to 6,910.39, more than 10% below its October record and its seventh straight loss. The index lost roughly **8.6%** on the week, its worst since April 2025, while the Nasdaq dropped about 10% and erased its 2026 gains. Anthropic's record IPO debut on Thursday failed to revive sentiment.

The VIX jumped to about **35.9**, its highest close since March, as the SOX semiconductor index fell 10.7% on the day. Contagion was global: the STOXX 600 lost about 5.8% on the week and the Nikkei roughly 7.7%. Haven flows pulled the 10-year UST yield down to around **4.95%** and lifted the JPY, though futures still price a December Fed hike at roughly 90%.

title: Nvidia sinks about 14% as SEC accounting probe overshadows record quarter
content:
Nvidia reported fiscal Q3 revenue of about $115.8bn on 18 November, up roughly 103% year on year and ahead of consensus near $108.8bn, and guided Q4 to around $130bn. Shares initially rose after hours, but gains faded amid leadership uncertainty under interim CEO Colette Kress. On 20 November, Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff were examining potential accounting issues, including changes to revenue reporting and AI financing deals.

The stock fell about **14%** on Friday to roughly **$125.53**, taking its weekly loss to around **23%**, its worst week since October 2008. As the AI bellwether, its slide dragged chipmakers lower from Wall Street to Tokyo and Seoul. Reuters noted that investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without enforcement action.

title: UK CPI rises to 3.6% but softer services trim BoE December hike bets; gilts rally
content:
UK CPI inflation rose to 3.6% in the 12 months to October from 3.5% in September, the ONS said, a one-year high driven mainly by fuel and an earlier tobacco duty rise. The print was slightly below the BoE's 3.7% forecast. Core CPI held at 2.8%, while services inflation stayed at 3.7%, under the Reuters poll forecast of 3.8%.

Markets trimmed the implied probability of a December BoE hike to about 80% from roughly 90% before the release. The 10-year gilt yield fell about **8–10bp** to near **5.29%**, while sterling slipped around 0.4% to about **$1.31**, a multi-week low. The MPC announces its decision on 17 December, a day after November CPI is published.
